newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's pegs Vietnam foreign currency ceiling Ba3.
newsitem.headline: Moody's pegs Vietnam foreign currency ceiling Ba3.

text.p: Moody's Investment Service said on Friday it had assigned a Ba3 country ceiling for ratings on long-term foreign-currency bonds and notes of issuers domciled in Vietnam, and a not prime ceiling for short-term obligations.
The rating agency said it expected to assign a Ba3 rating to the forthcoming Eurobond to be issued by Vietnam.
Moody's said in a statement it also assigned a B1 country ceiling for ratings of foreign currency-denominated bank deposits.

The ratings were supported by Vietnam's track record of structural reform and macro-economic stabilisation, its robust investment- and export-led growth and success in restructuring its external debt burden, the rating agency said.
Vietnam's commitment to integrate the country into the international economic system was demonstrated by its progress in normalising economic and political relations with the United States, it said.
However, a low domestic saving rate, weak legal and administrative systems, massive infrastructure needs, a fragile financial sector and undeveloped capital markets offset the rating, Moody's said.

In addition, it said the rapid buildup in short-term debt has been accompanied by certain payment irregularities within the financial system. This raised concern over the relatively low level of official foreign exchange reserves and the overall strength of the country's external payments position.
